metadata.title: Discourse of contemporary chinese ideological and political education: Development directions and teaching methods

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study collected primary survey and interview data from a single prestigious Chinese university (metropolis with >11 million inhabitants) using an adapted questionnaire based on the IEA ICCS framework and the Citizenship Education Longitudinal Study (CELS). The manuscript does not report the use of complex survey sampling weights (e.g., student design weights) or any replicate-weight procedures; instead, it reports simple descriptive statistics and inferential tests (t-tests, regression) on the obtained volunteer sample. Because the analysis is not conducted on an ILSA microdata file with stratified multistage sampling, there is no documented weight variable to apply for population-representative estimation. The analytic sample was formed by invitation (200 invitations), yielding 182 participants, and then excluding 10 incomplete responses; no additional outlier trimming or imputation procedures are described.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The study does not use ILSA cognitive achievement scores with Plausible Values; instead, it analyzes students’ perceptions and self-reported civic intention/participation using Likert-scale items and derived indices. Missing-data handling is not reported beyond discarding incomplete responses, and the paper does not describe an imputation or formal missing-data protocol for item nonresponse. Given the non-PV, questionnaire-based dependent variables, PV handling is not applicable by design.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were Chinese undergraduate students at one university who were required to take political/ideological education courses. Invitations were sent to third- and fourth-year students via email; 182 participants were included in the final sample. Eight invitees did not participate after invitation, and 10 incomplete responses were discarded. The study further describes disciplinary composition (foreign languages/literature, arts, economics & management, physics & technology) and geographic diversity across 9 provinces, but it does not report additional item-level exclusions or imputation rules.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICCS the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that This paper evaluates teaching methods and perceived outcomes of ideological and political education among Chinese university students using a questionnaire adapted from the IEA ICCS model and supplemented by interviews. The study’s quantitative results are based on Likert-scale indices and descriptive distributions (e.g., method usage frequencies) plus inferential statistics (single-sample t-tests and a simple regression), not on machine-learning prediction of an achievement outcome. The reported metrics are mainly mean differences from a test value (e.g., trust and civic intention means significantly above 3 with p<.01 or p<.001) and a regression result showing Political Theory explaining 12.6% of variance in socio-political activity (R²=0.126; Beta=0.355; p<.001). The best-performing “model” in an ML sense is not applicable because no ML algorithms are trained or compared. Limitations include a single-university convenience sample, no survey-weight documentation, and no PV-based achievement measurement. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an empirical survey/interview study with questionnaire-based Likert outcomes and basic statistical testing; it does not perform machine-learning model training/prediction, does not use ILSA cognitive achievement Plausible Values, and does not report an ML pipeline. Therefore, fields related to ML techniques and PV handling are intentionally empty or set to not_applicable, and no country-level ILSA cycle/grade/domain can be extracted because the data are not an ICCS/PV microdata analysis.
